Claude Code is a terminal session that can read this repository,
edit it, and run `uv`. Start it in the project root, not in your
home directory. The commands below are the ones worth keeping from
the Real Python
[Claude Code cheat sheet](https://realpython.com/cheatsheets/claude-code/):
how to spend fewer tokens, how to drop a finished chat, and how to
load a skill. The printed sheet is embedded at the end.

```bash
cd my-project/                 # directory that holds pyproject.toml
claude                         # interactive session
claude "explain this repo"     # one prompt, then the session
```

In this course that directory is the repository root, after
`uv sync`. Type `/` to list commands.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## What happens when you press Enter

![One request through Claude Code, from prompt to final message. © ByteByteGo, reproduced for teaching ([source](https://blog.bytebytego.com/)).](claude_code_agent.jpg){#fig-claude-loop fig-alt="Flow diagram: the user prompt goes through the interface to the agent loop, which proposes an edit; the permission system checks it; a tool runs it in the execution environment; the result returns to the agent loop, which updates memory and replies to the user."}

@fig-claude-loop follows one prompt, "Fix the failing test in
auth.test.ts":

1. You send the prompt through your interface.
2. The interface (CLI, IDE, or SDK) adds the repository and file
   context and passes the request to the agent loop.
3. The agent loop plans the next move and proposes an action:
   `Edit(auth.ts, lines 42–55)`.
4. The permission system checks that action against the allow, ask,
   and deny rules (@sec-claude-permissions).
5. The approved action becomes a tool call, `Edit(auth.ts, patch)`,
   sent to the matching tool.
6. The tool runs in the execution environment (shell, cloud, or
   sandbox) as a real system call.
7. The execution returns a tool result to the agent loop.
8. The agent saves the turn to its state and streams the final
   message to you.

Steps 3 to 7 repeat until the task is done. Each pass adds the tool
result to the context, which is why long tasks cost more tokens
(@sec-claude-tokens). The numbers in the picture differ slightly:
it numbers the tool call 4 and leaves the permission check
unnumbered.
:::

## Slash commands worth keeping {#sec-claude-slash}

Put the command at the start of the message. `/compact` shortens the
chat so you can continue. `/clear` throws the chat away when the
task changes. `/skills` is how a `SKILL.md` becomes a command.

| Command | What it does |
|---------|----------------|
| `/context` | Show how much of the window is in use |
| `/compact [focus]` | Summarise the chat and free space |
| `/clear` | Start a fresh chat. Also `/new` |
| `/usage` | Show cost and limits. Also `/cost` |
| `/effort low` | Set effort. `high` spends more tokens |
| `/model [name]` | Switch model. `s` in the picker is this session only |
| `/skills` | List skills and turn them on or off |
| `/reload-skills` | Load skills added during the session |

`/memory`, `/hooks`, `/permissions`, and `/mcp` open the four
configurations in the rest of this page.

## Three scopes {#sec-claude-scopes}

The same choice comes up for memory, for the settings file that
holds hooks and permissions, and for skills.

| Scope | Memory | Hooks and permissions | Skills |
|-------|--------|------------------------|--------|
| You, every project | `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` | `~/.claude/settings.json` | `~/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` |
| This project, the team | `CLAUDE.md` (commit it) | `.claude/settings.json` | `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` |
| This project, only you | `CLAUDE.local.md` | `.claude/settings.local.json` | No third directory |

Commit the team row. The "only you" row is gitignored in this
repository. The cheat sheet does not give skills a third path: a
skill that must not be shared belongs in `~/.claude/skills/`. If it
has to sit inside the project, gitignore that one skill directory.

Settings files are strict JSON: no comments, no trailing commas.
List keys such as `permissions.allow` merge across files. Managed
settings win, then a `--settings` file, then local, project, and
user. `/status` shows which files loaded. All `CLAUDE.md` files
load together, from broad to specific, so do not leave two files
disagreeing. From Claude Code v2.1.277, `AGENTS.md` loads when a
repository has no `CLAUDE.md`.

::: {.callout-note}
## Personal files stay off Git

`.gitignore` lists `CLAUDE.local.md` and
`.claude/settings.local.json`. `CLAUDE.md`,
`.claude/settings.json`, `.claude/skills/`, and `.mcp.json` are
the files the team shares.
:::

## Hooks {#sec-claude-hooks}

A hook is a command that runs at a fixed point in the loop. `/hooks`
lists what is registered. Exit code 2 from `PreToolUse` blocks the
tool call. Put the JSON in the settings file for the scope you
chose.

| Event | When it runs |
|-------|----------------|
| `SessionStart` | The session begins or resumes |
| `UserPromptSubmit` | Before Claude sees your prompt |
| `PreToolUse` | Before a tool runs. Can block it |
| `PostToolUse` | After a tool succeeds |
| `Notification` | Claude needs your input |
| `Stop` | Claude has finished replying |

This hook formats the tree with Ruff after every edit or write,
which matches the `uv` / Ruff setup in this repository:

```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PostToolUse": [{
      "matcher": "Edit|Write",
      "hooks": [{
        "type": "command",
        "command": "ruff format ."
      }]
    }]
  }
}
```

## Memory {#sec-claude-memory}

`CLAUDE.md` is what you write. Auto memory is what Claude writes.
`/memory` opens the files. A file can pull others in with `@`:

```markdown
# Project Notes
See @README.md for an overview.
- Testing: @docs/testing.md
- Mine: @~/.claude/my-notes.md
```

A rule under `.claude/rules/` can apply only to some paths. This
one is loaded for Python under `src/api/`:

```markdown
---
paths:
  - "src/api/**/*.py"
---
- Validate every request body
```

`/init` drafts a first `CLAUDE.md` for the repository.

## Spend fewer tokens {#sec-claude-tokens}

Every turn resends the system prompt, the `CLAUDE.md` files and
rules, the tool schemas, and the chat so far. @fig-token-cost lists
six ways to cut that cost in any LLM system.

![Six cost-reduction techniques for LLM systems. © ByteByteGo, reproduced for teaching ([source](https://blog.bytebytego.com/)).](token_code_optimisation.jpg){#fig-token-cost fig-alt="Table of six techniques with a workflow sketch each: prompt caching, model routing, batch API, semantic cache, trimming the context, and smaller models."}

| Technique | What it does | In my setup |
|-----------|--------------|-------------|
| Prompt caching | Reuses the computation for a prefix that does not change | Automatic. Rules, `CLAUDE.md` and the MCP list stay unchanged during a session |
| Model routing | Easy requests go to a small model, hard ones to a large model | A `token-budget` rule says which model does what; a Haiku agent does document search |
| Batch API | Sends many requests as one asynchronous job, at a discount | Not used interactively. Kept for scripted bulk extraction |
| Semantic cache | Reuses a stored answer for a similar question | `doc-search note`: checked answers, matched by question similarity |
| Trim the context | Sends only what the next step needs | Path-scoped rules, 3–5 excerpts per search, subagent briefs, `/clear` |
| Go smaller | Distilled or quantised models for narrow tasks | Haiku for retrieval, a local MiniLM model for embeddings, `/effort low` |

The rest of this section shows each choice. The files are in
[`python/doc-search/`](https://github.com/bastienchassagnol/Rag-llm-playground/tree/main/python/doc-search).

### What a month costs {#sec-claude-cost}

Claude Code writes every response, with its token counts, to
`~/.claude/projects/*/*.jsonl`. Over 30 days (25 active days) of
course and tooling work, one user consumed:

| Token type | 30 days | Share |
|------------|--------:|------:|
| Cache reads | 1.94 billion | 97 % |
| Cache writes | 55 million | 2.7 % |
| Output | 7.4 million | 0.4 % |
| Fresh input | 14 thousand | < 0.01 % |

Cache reads are billed at about a tenth of the input price, so
the raw total of 2 billion overstates the cost. The lesson is
that the stable prefix is re-read on every turn: a shorter prefix
and fewer turns save more than shorter prompts. `/usage` gives the
plan view; this script gives the split by type:

```python
import collections, glob, json, os

seen, total = set(), collections.Counter()
for f in glob.glob(os.path.expanduser("~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl"), recursive=True):
    for line in open(f, errors="ignore"):
        msg = json.loads(line).get("message") or {}
        if not isinstance(msg, dict) or "usage" not in msg or msg.get("id") in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(msg.get("id"))
        total.update({k: v for k, v in msg["usage"].items() if isinstance(v, int)})
print(total)
```

### Rules and models {#sec-claude-routing}

- **Path-scoped rules.** Long user rules (figures, LaTeX, document
  extraction, symbolic verification) start with `paths:`, so they
  load only when Claude opens a matching file
  (@sec-claude-memory). A short index in `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` says
  which rule to read when no file triggers it, for example a PDF
  searched through `doc-search`.
- **One short rule always on.**
  [`token-budget.md`](https://github.com/bastienchassagnol/Rag-llm-playground/blob/main/python/doc-search/token-budget.md) routes tasks:
  Haiku for search and formatting, Sonnet for routine edits, Opus
  for design, statistical review and synthesis. It also says when
  to save an answer and why rules must not change mid-session.
- **A Haiku agent for reading.**
  [`doc-retriever.md`](https://github.com/bastienchassagnol/Rag-llm-playground/blob/main/python/doc-search/doc-retriever.md) in
  `~/.claude/agents/` searches one document and returns quoted
  excerpts and a brief of at most 500 words. With several
  documents, Claude starts one per file and reads only the briefs.

  ```markdown
  ---
  name: doc-retriever
  tools: Bash, Read, Grep, Glob
  model: haiku
  ---
  ```

- **Smallest code change.** The
  [Ponytail](https://github.com/DietrichGebert/ponytail) rule (MIT)
  is scoped to code files. It asks for the shortest complete
  change and a closing line on what was not checked, which keeps
  both the diff and the output short.
- **Effort per model.** `modelSettings` in `~/.claude/settings.json`
  sets a default effort for each model; `/effort low` overrides it
  for mechanical edits.

### Retrieval with doc-search {#sec-claude-docsearch}

[`doc_search.py`](https://github.com/bastienchassagnol/Rag-llm-playground/blob/main/python/doc-search/doc_search.py) keeps PDFs, Word,
PowerPoint, HTML and Markdown files on disk and returns a few
sourced excerpts instead of whole documents. It runs with
`uv run --script` and needs Docling (`uv tool install docling`)
and poppler.

```bash
doc_search.py index paper.pdf
doc_search.py search "prior on the dispersion" --source paper.pdf
doc_search.py search "dispersion" --regex 'theta_?\d' -i
doc_search.py search "estimand" --whole-section
doc_search.py note add --source paper.pdf --pages 7-8 \
  --question "What is the primary estimand?" --answer "..."
doc_search.py figures paper.pdf --slug smith2024
```

- **Chunks follow sections.** Docling's hybrid chunker never crosses
  a heading and caps each chunk at 256 tokens. That is the window
  of the embedding model (all-MiniLM-L6-v2): the earlier
  2,000-character chunks, about 500 tokens, had their second half
  ignored. `--whole-section` prints a hit's full section.
- **Each excerpt says where it is from.** The output gives `SOURCE`,
  `PAGES`, `SECTION` (the heading path) and `RANKS`, so a quote can
  be cited without opening the file.
- **Meaning, keywords and patterns together.** Three rankings are
  merged by weighted reciprocal-rank fusion: embeddings (Chroma),
  BM25 keywords (SQLite FTS5), and match counts for `--regex`. The
  default weights are 1, 1 and 2, because a pattern you type is a
  strong signal. Symbols, gene names and citekeys need the regex.
- **Answers are cached.** After Claude has checked an answer against
  its excerpts, `note add` stores it. A later search whose question
  is similar (cosine similarity ≥ 0.90) prints the cached note and
  stops. Re-indexing a changed file deletes its notes.
- **Figures come out automatically.** `figures` finds the pages
  whose text starts a line with "Figure N" or "Fig. N", saves every
  embedded image with `pdfimages -png -p`, renders those pages at
  200 dpi with `pdftoppm`, and lists them in
  `.firecrawl/extract/<slug>/figure-candidates.json`. On a two-page
  paper (ImmQuant, Frishberg et al. 2016) it found Fig. 1 on
  page 2. Choosing and describing the figures stays a reading
  task, done after looking at each image.

Other savings: run `/context` before `/compact`, turn off unused
servers in `/mcp`, and use `/clear` between unrelated tasks
(@sec-claude-slash). Long procedures belong in a skill, whose body
loads only when it runs (@sec-claude-skills).

## Skills {#sec-claude-skills}

A directory with a `SKILL.md` becomes `/name`. Claude also loads
the skill when the description matches the task. Set
`disable-model-invocation: true` when the skill should run only
if you type the command. Older `.claude/commands/*.md` files still
work. After you add a skill, run `/reload-skills` if the session
was already open.

```markdown
---
name: docstring-doctor
description: >-
  Writes Google-style Python docstrings.
  Use when asked to document code.
---
Open with a one-line summary...
```

The instructions under the front matter are what Claude follows
each time the skill runs.

## Permissions {#sec-claude-permissions}

`Shift+Tab` cycles `default`, `acceptEdits`, and `plan`, and
`auto` when that mode is available. Since v2.1.283, most terminal
and VS Code sessions start in `auto`. The interface labels
`default` as Manual. `/permissions` edits the rules. Rules are
checked deny, then ask, then allow. The first match wins. A deny
rule still holds in `bypassPermissions`.

| Mode | Runs without asking |
|------|---------------------|
| `default` | Reads only |
| `acceptEdits` | Reads, edits, file commands |
| `plan` | Reads, to draft a plan |
| `auto` | Everything, with safety checks |
| `dontAsk` | Pre-approved tools and file reads |
| `bypassPermissions` | Everything, in isolated VMs |

For this repository, allow the test command, ask before a push,
and refuse the env file:

```json
{
  "permissions": {
    "allow": ["Bash(uv run pytest *)"],
    "ask": ["Bash(git push *)"],
    "deny": ["Read(./.env)"]
  }
}
```

## MCP servers {#sec-claude-mcp}

MCP connects the session to tools outside the chat. `/mcp` manages
servers and OAuth logins. Scopes are `local`, `project`, and
`user`. `local` is the default and stays out of the shared file.
`project` writes `.mcp.json`, which the team commits. `user`
follows you across repositories. For a stdio server, `--` comes
before the process Claude should launch. Point a database server
at a read-only user.

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http \
  notion https://mcp.notion.com/mcp
claude mcp add --transport stdio \
  --scope project db \
  -- npx -y @bytebase/dbhub \
  --dsn "postgresql://readonly:pw@host/db"
```

The same stdio form can launch this course's server from the
repository root:

```bash
claude mcp add --transport stdio \
  --scope project course \
  -- uv run python python/basic-mcp-server/server.py
```

That server is the one in
[a minimal MCP server](basic-mcp-server.qmd). List, inspect, and
remove servers from the shell:

```bash
claude mcp list
claude mcp get notion
claude mcp remove notion
```

Server prompts show up in the `/` menu as `/server:prompt`.
